title: Sum of Values at Indices With K Set Bits
statement: Given an integer array `nums` (indexed from 0) and an integer `k`, add up every `nums[i]` whose index `i`, written in binary, contains exactly `k` ones, and return that sum. If no index qualifies, the sum is `0`.
notes:
## Intuition

The values themselves never matter for the decision; only the index does. So walk the indices, count the ones in each index's binary form, and add the value when that count is exactly `k`. Counting bits can be done without converting to a string: `rest & (rest - 1)` clears the lowest one bit, so the number of times you can do that before reaching 0 is the number of ones.

## Approach

1. Start `total` at 0.
2. For each index `i`, copy it into `rest` and set `bits` to 0.
3. While `rest` is not 0, clear its lowest set bit with `rest &= rest - 1` and add one to `bits`.
4. If `bits` equals `k`, add `nums[i]` to `total`.
5. Return `total`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [5, 10, 1, 5, 2]`, `k = 1`. Index 0 has `bits = 0` (skip). Index 1 (`1`) has 1 bit, so `total = 10`. Index 2 (`10`) has 1 bit, so `total = 11`. Index 3 (`11`) has 2 bits (skip). Index 4 (`100`) has 1 bit, so `total = 13`. The answer is `13`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n): each index needs at most about log n bit-clearing steps.
- Space: O(1): only a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- Count bits of the **index** `i`, not of the value `nums[i]`.
- Index 0 has zero set bits, so with `k = 0` the answer is `nums[0]`.
- With at most 1000 indices no index has 10 set bits, so `k = 10` gives `0`; do not assume some index always matches.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `total` | running sum of the chosen values |
| `i` | the current index |
| `rest` | what is left of `i` while its bits are being cleared |
| `bits` | number of set bits counted in `i` so far |

narration.3: Visit every index; the decision depends only on the index.
narration.5: Work on a copy of the index so i itself is untouched.
narration.6: Keep going while the copy still has a set bit.
narration.7: rest & (rest - 1) removes exactly the lowest set bit.
narration.8: Each removal accounts for one set bit.
narration.10: Does this index have exactly k set bits?
narration.11: Yes: include its value in the sum.
narration.14: Every index has been checked; return the sum.
